beforeClose.title: Append-only scope remediation and recertification
beforeClose.objective: Safely remediate and recertify closed Kyro scopes without changing immutable checkpoint history.
successCriteria: An operator can preview and atomically apply a typed remediation to a closed scope without altering historical checkpoint bytes or commitments.
Every remediation records its affected issues, typed operations, source commitments, and corrected-state digest in an append-only chain.
Artifact Doctor distinguishes historical, remediated, recertified, diverged, and unsupported scope states.
A scope is not reported as recertified unless an immutable certification record validates the remediation and checker evidence.
Lens loads valid remediation chains with provenance and rejects invalid or unsupported chains without silently using stale state.

requirements.statement: The system must preserve every original checkpoint, snapshot, narrative, and ledger commitment while a closed scope is remediated.
requirements.rationale: Historical evidence must remain tamper-evident; remediation cannot rewrite the event it corrects.

requirements.statement: The system must represent each remediation as a versioned record with base state digest, affected checkpoint commitments, issues, typed operations, provenance, and expected result digest.
requirements.rationale: A remediation must be auditable and bound to the exact state it corrects.

requirements.statement: The system must accept only operations from a closed typed registry and reject arbitrary patch instructions.
requirements.rationale: Strong typing prevents semantic rewriting of tasks, evidence, checkpoints, or credentials. The first operation is debt.origin.set.

requirements.statement: The system must preview and apply a remediation batch atomically, failing without writes when any digest, precondition, operation, schema, or post-write verification fails.
requirements.rationale: A partially corrected closed scope is less trustworthy than an explicitly blocked one.

requirements.statement: The system must validate and expose the remediation chain independently from historical checkpoint integrity.
requirements.rationale: Doctor and status must report remediated, recertified, diverged, and unsupported states truthfully.

requirements.statement: The system must create a separate immutable recertification record only when a valid remediation chain and checker validation evidence are present.
requirements.rationale: Applying a correction is not equivalent to certifying the corrected scope.

requirements.statement: Kyro Lens must load and present valid remediation and recertification provenance while failing closed for invalid or unsupported protocol versions.
requirements.rationale: The reader that exposed the original contract violation must consume the new protocol safely.

scenarios.when: Kyro evaluates it

scenarios.then: both report the identical worst applicable state by the precedence diverged > unsupported > remediated > recertified > historical, with the same detail naming the specific reason

scenarios.when: Kyro Lens loads the scope through its read-only workspace reader

scenarios.when: Kyro Lens loads the scope
scenarios.then: Lens fails closed with an actionable diverged or unsupported diagnostic and never substitutes the historical checkpoint or stale state as valid current provenance

scenarios.when: Lens loads the workspace through either supported reader

scenarios.when: Kyro Lens evaluates provenance

scenarios.when: Lens builds assistant context
scenarios.then: it includes at most a bounded derived provenance summary and never forwards raw remediation snapshots, raw record bytes, or evidence contents

scenarios.given: self-contained Lens fixtures generated and committed from a real Kyro v1 close, remediate, and recertify flow
scenarios.when: Lens runs typecheck, build, and tests in its isolated CI checkout
scenarios.then: the valid and invalid contract cases run without a sibling Kyro AI checkout while a separate cross-repository gate can regenerate and compare the fixture provenance

nonGoals: Generic JSON Patch or arbitrary field mutation.
Automatic conversion of semantically ambiguous historical values.
Rewriting checkpoints, snapshots, narratives, ledger commitments, task evidence, or verdicts.
Restoring missing checkpoint bytes from Git or backup.
Claiming production readiness from local recertification.

adrs.title: Recertification evidence must have a verifiable trust root
adrs.context: The Sprint 2 plan let kyro recertify accept a passing checker verdict without defining where that verdict comes from. A verdict string supplied by the same manifest that requests the certificate is the requester certifying itself, which is exactly the class of unearned trust this scope exists to prevent. Sprint 1 already showed the cost: a hand-written remediation record with digests matching nothing flipped doctor from DIVERGED to certified until the chain was replayed rather than believed.
adrs.decision: A certification records evidence as typed entries, each carrying a source, an identity, a content digest, and the chain head commitment it was produced against. Two sources are valid in v1: a Kyro task verdict, referenced by scope, task id and the digest of the recorded verdict object, which Kyro re-reads and re-verifies from sprint.json rather than trusting the manifest copy; and an external artifact, referenced by a path inside the workspace plus its sha256, which Kyro re-hashes at verification time. Any evidence entry whose digest does not reproduce, or whose chain head is not the current head, invalidates the whole certification. A bare pass string with no verifiable source is rejected.
consequences: kyro recertify cannot be satisfied by manifest-declared assertions alone; every claim it certifies is independently re-derivable from artifacts Kyro can read.
A certificate is bound to one chain head, so remediating again after certification necessarily drops the scope out of recertified rather than silently carrying the old certificate forward.
External evidence must live inside the workspace so its digest can be re-verified; evidence outside it cannot be certified in v1.
alternatives: Accept a manifest-supplied verdict string and rely on operator discipline — rejected, it certifies nothing and is indistinguishable from a forged claim.
Require a live re-run of the checker during recertify — rejected for v1, it couples certification to executable test infrastructure and makes the record non-reproducible.

adrs.title: Composite verification states resolve by fail-closed precedence
adrs.context: The state vocabulary in T2.1 was specified as five names without saying what happens when several apply at once: an unsupported schemaVersion together with an invalid digest, a valid certificate over a chain that later diverged, an unreadable record behind a well-formed anchor. Left undefined, doctor and status can each pick a different answer for the same scope, and the more reassuring one tends to win. Sprint 1 produced exactly that failure twice, in both directions.
adrs.decision: The five states are strictly ordered and the WORST applicable state always wins: diverged > unsupported > remediated > recertified > historical. Concretely, an unreadable or contract-invalid record behind a valid anchor is diverged, not unsupported, because unreadability cannot be distinguished from tampering; an unknown schemaVersion with otherwise intact digests is unsupported, because this runtime cannot judge it; a valid certificate whose chain head no longer matches the live chain is diverged, never recertified; and recertified requires remediated to hold first. Doctor and status derive the state from one shared function so they cannot disagree, and each reports the same detail string naming the specific reason.
consequences: No combination of conditions can produce a more reassuring state than its worst component, which removes the whole class of defects where hardening one path let another path certify.
recertified is never reachable without a currently valid chain, so a certificate cannot outlive the state it certified.
Callers get one state and one reason rather than a set, which keeps status output and Lens ingestion simple in Sprint 3.
alternatives: Report every applicable state as a set and let the reader decide — rejected, it pushes the trust decision onto the least informed layer.
Treat unreadable records as unsupported rather than diverged — rejected, it lets deleting or corrupting bytes downgrade a failure into a benign-looking one.

adrs.title: Replay must start from the live base a remediation actually corrected
adrs.context: Sprint 2 QA reproduced a genuine two-record chain (R-001 prose->1 on a scope whose live debt origin was corrupted after close, then R-002 1->2) being reported diverged by both doctor and status. resolveRemediationRebase replays from checkpoint.intendedAfterClose, but the first record's base is the DRIFTED live state — the corruption is exactly the reason to remediate — so the replay can only close when the pre-remediation live state already equalled the after-image. Both records report APPLIED individually yet the whole scope is diverged. The Sprint 1 harness hides this because every multi-record case hand-resets debt[0].origin=1 before remediating, so the first base coincides with the after-image by construction.
adrs.decision: The replay remains the trust root (T2.1 finding 1 is deliberately not fixed in T2.1), but a genuine chain whose first record's base is the drifted live state must still certify. Concretely: resolveRemediationRebase must prove the first record's base is consistent with the live state it was built against rather than demanding it equal the checkpoint after-image, while still failing closed on hand-written records whose digests correspond to no state Kyro can reproduce. The existing QA probes (forged chain, no-op remediation over tampered state) define the attack boundary that any fix must keep failing closed.
consequences: A scope whose corruption predates its first remediation can present an honest multi-record chain as remediated instead of diverged.

The fix touches Sprint 1 replay code shared by doctor and the T2.1 derivation, so it must be validated with honest-path multi-record probes from a genuinely drifted base, not just the after-image-aligned fixtures.
alternatives: Relax the derivation to accept any per-record-APPLIED chain without replay — rejected, it lets a hand-written record whose base digests match nothing certify a diverged scope, which is exactly the QA probe 2 defect from Sprint 1.

Keep the strict after-image replay and document that legitimate first-record drift is unrepresentable — rejected, it makes the motivating case (corrupt-after-close) permanently divergent and forces operators to fabricate an after-image-aligned base.

adrs.title: Conform Lens provenance verification to Kyro v1 vectors
adrs.context: Lens must report valid remediation and recertification provenance without reusing the mutable Kyro runtime or trusting anchors alone.
adrs.decision: Lens implements a strict v1 verifier with canonical SHA-256 and checked-in real Kyro conformance vectors; cryptographic unavailability or any unsupported condition is reported as unsupported, and valid provenance is not inferred from anchor shape alone.
consequences: Reader-specific loading stays read-only and deterministic while verification semantics are explicit and regression-tested across runtimes.
The initial Lens verifier covers only declared v1 vectors; protocol evolution requires new vectors and an explicit version decision.
alternatives: Trust the anchor fields without verifying record, evidence, and chain semantics.
Import Kyro AI source or require a sibling checkout in Lens CI.

roadmap.sizingRationale: Three sprints isolate the persistence/security foundation, the verification and certification semantics, and the cross-repository Lens reader contract. Fewer sprints would mix irreversible writer behavior with its auditor and reader; more would create artificial boundaries. Sprint 2 depends on Sprint 1's stable remediation schema, and Sprint 3 depends on the finalized Doctor/status protocol.

sprints.title: Typed remediation protocol and atomic writer

recommendations: Sprint 2 (R5) should replace the current binary checkpoint verdict with the real state vocabulary: historical, remediated, recertified, diverged, unsupported. Today a legacy checkpoint that embeds a value the current schema rejects stays permanently invalid to doctor even after its live state is correctly remediated.
kyro recertify (R6) closes debt-1: check:cli-verbs fails only on that unshipped verb referenced in docs/plans/append-only-scope-remediation.md.

Before Lens ingestion (R7), confirm Lens resolves remediation records through remediations[].path — E3 made that field authoritative by binding it to the anchor id, and the reader must agree with doctor about which file is the evidence.
Re-run an independent QA certification of this scope when budget allows; the closing audit was performed by the same session that wrote the code.

Resolve debt-2 first: verify stateDigest(record.result.snapshot) === record.result.stateSha256 inside the replay loop, or drop snapshot and replay from the computed next state. It is not exploitable today only because chainContinuityIssue runs first.
Certify a global install, not just the local checkout. The installed runtime did not surface the verification state, which is what made the active-sprint false DIVERGED easy to miss.
Close S3/Lens and the R7 coverage that analyze still reports as pending before certifying the scope end to end.

tasks.title: Resolve and verify anchored provenance in Lens
tasks.description: Implement the read-only resolver that follows each remediation anchor through remediations[].path and validates its identity, scope containment, commitment, ordering, certificate chain-head binding, and evidence references before producing a Lens provenance summary.
tasks.context: The remediation anchor path is authoritative only when it is scope-contained and names the same R-NNN id as the anchor; Lens must not discover alternate files or silently select a different record. Reuse Kyro AI's canonical commitment rules through shared contract fixtures, not a looser reader-only interpretation. Records and evidence are read only and are never applied, repaired, or rewritten by Lens.
acceptance_criteria: A valid ordered chain resolves to a provenance summary containing the historical issue, remediation rationale, typed operations, current verification state, and optional certification.

Path traversal, anchor/id disagreement, content or commitment mismatch, broken chain order, stale certificate head, unreadable evidence, and unsupported version return an actionable integrity or unsupported result.
The Lens corpus includes validated remediation and certification artifacts when present and records a read failure instead of inventing content when they are not valid.
The resolver performs no workspace writes.

emergentTasks.title: Verify Lens v1 provenance against canonical vectors
emergentTasks.description: Correct T3.3 by implementing a strict, read-only v1 verifier instead of trusting an anchor-shaped record. It must use canonical JSON and SHA-256, exact closed-record validation, record and anchor containment rules, evidence semantics, and real Kyro conformance vectors before Lens may claim verified remediation or recertification provenance.
emergentTasks.context: Implements ADR-0004 and S14. This replaces the loose reader-only interpretation implied by T3.3 with an explicitly conformant v1 verifier.
acceptance_criteria: Lens accepts only v1 closed record shapes and lower-case 64-hex digests; unknown keys or versions, unavailable cryptography, bad commitment, broken record ordering, and stale certificate head are unsupported or diverged, never valid.

Remediation and certification records and their anchors are scope-contained archive references with matching identities; external artifact evidence is workspace-contained, while kyro-task-verdict evidence is re-derived from the current sprint state.

Canonical SHA-256 and state/chain evaluation match checked-in real Kyro conformance vectors including a genuine divergence and an active later sprint; Lens never labels a chain remediated or recertified based only on anchor shape.
The verifier and all readers remain read-only.

intendedAfterClose.title: Append-only scope remediation and recertification
intendedAfterClose.objective: Safely remediate and recertify closed Kyro scopes without changing immutable checkpoint history.
successCriteria: An operator can preview and atomically apply a typed remediation to a closed scope without altering historical checkpoint bytes or commitments.
Every remediation records its affected issues, typed operations, source commitments, and corrected-state digest in an append-only chain.
Artifact Doctor distinguishes historical, remediated, recertified, diverged, and unsupported scope states.
A scope is not reported as recertified unless an immutable certification record validates the remediation and checker evidence.
Lens loads valid remediation chains with provenance and rejects invalid or unsupported chains without silently using stale state.

requirements.statement: The system must preserve every original checkpoint, snapshot, narrative, and ledger commitment while a closed scope is remediated.
requirements.rationale: Historical evidence must remain tamper-evident; remediation cannot rewrite the event it corrects.

requirements.statement: The system must represent each remediation as a versioned record with base state digest, affected checkpoint commitments, issues, typed operations, provenance, and expected result digest.
requirements.rationale: A remediation must be auditable and bound to the exact state it corrects.

requirements.statement: The system must accept only operations from a closed typed registry and reject arbitrary patch instructions.
requirements.rationale: Strong typing prevents semantic rewriting of tasks, evidence, checkpoints, or credentials. The first operation is debt.origin.set.

requirements.statement: The system must preview and apply a remediation batch atomically, failing without writes when any digest, precondition, operation, schema, or post-write verification fails.
requirements.rationale: A partially corrected closed scope is less trustworthy than an explicitly blocked one.

requirements.statement: The system must validate and expose the remediation chain independently from historical checkpoint integrity.
requirements.rationale: Doctor and status must report remediated, recertified, diverged, and unsupported states truthfully.

requirements.statement: The system must create a separate immutable recertification record only when a valid remediation chain and checker validation evidence are present.
requirements.rationale: Applying a correction is not equivalent to certifying the corrected scope.

requirements.statement: Kyro Lens must load and present valid remediation and recertification provenance while failing closed for invalid or unsupported protocol versions.
requirements.rationale: The reader that exposed the original contract violation must consume the new protocol safely.

adrs.title: Recertification evidence must have a verifiable trust root
adrs.context: The Sprint 2 plan let kyro recertify accept a passing checker verdict without defining where that verdict comes from. A verdict string supplied by the same manifest that requests the certificate is the requester certifying itself, which is exactly the class of unearned trust this scope exists to prevent. Sprint 1 already showed the cost: a hand-written remediation record with digests matching nothing flipped doctor from DIVERGED to certified until the chain was replayed rather than believed.
adrs.decision: A certification records evidence as typed entries, each carrying a source, an identity, a content digest, and the chain head commitment it was produced against. Two sources are valid in v1: a Kyro task verdict, referenced by scope, task id and the digest of the recorded verdict object, which Kyro re-reads and re-verifies from sprint.json rather than trusting the manifest copy; and an external artifact, referenced by a path inside the workspace plus its sha256, which Kyro re-hashes at verification time. Any evidence entry whose digest does not reproduce, or whose chain head is not the current head, invalidates the whole certification. A bare pass string with no verifiable source is rejected.
consequences: kyro recertify cannot be satisfied by manifest-declared assertions alone; every claim it certifies is independently re-derivable from artifacts Kyro can read.
A certificate is bound to one chain head, so remediating again after certification necessarily drops the scope out of recertified rather than silently carrying the old certificate forward.
External evidence must live inside the workspace so its digest can be re-verified; evidence outside it cannot be certified in v1.
alternatives: Accept a manifest-supplied verdict string and rely on operator discipline — rejected, it certifies nothing and is indistinguishable from a forged claim.
Require a live re-run of the checker during recertify — rejected for v1, it couples certification to executable test infrastructure and makes the record non-reproducible.

adrs.title: Composite verification states resolve by fail-closed precedence
adrs.context: The state vocabulary in T2.1 was specified as five names without saying what happens when several apply at once: an unsupported schemaVersion together with an invalid digest, a valid certificate over a chain that later diverged, an unreadable record behind a well-formed anchor. Left undefined, doctor and status can each pick a different answer for the same scope, and the more reassuring one tends to win. Sprint 1 produced exactly that failure twice, in both directions.
adrs.decision: The five states are strictly ordered and the WORST applicable state always wins: diverged > unsupported > remediated > recertified > historical. Concretely, an unreadable or contract-invalid record behind a valid anchor is diverged, not unsupported, because unreadability cannot be distinguished from tampering; an unknown schemaVersion with otherwise intact digests is unsupported, because this runtime cannot judge it; a valid certificate whose chain head no longer matches the live chain is diverged, never recertified; and recertified requires remediated to hold first. Doctor and status derive the state from one shared function so they cannot disagree, and each reports the same detail string naming the specific reason.
consequences: No combination of conditions can produce a more reassuring state than its worst component, which removes the whole class of defects where hardening one path let another path certify.
recertified is never reachable without a currently valid chain, so a certificate cannot outlive the state it certified.
Callers get one state and one reason rather than a set, which keeps status output and Lens ingestion simple in Sprint 3.
alternatives: Report every applicable state as a set and let the reader decide — rejected, it pushes the trust decision onto the least informed layer.
Treat unreadable records as unsupported rather than diverged — rejected, it lets deleting or corrupting bytes downgrade a failure into a benign-looking one.

adrs.title: Replay must start from the live base a remediation actually corrected
adrs.context: Sprint 2 QA reproduced a genuine two-record chain (R-001 prose->1 on a scope whose live debt origin was corrupted after close, then R-002 1->2) being reported diverged by both doctor and status. resolveRemediationRebase replays from checkpoint.intendedAfterClose, but the first record's base is the DRIFTED live state — the corruption is exactly the reason to remediate — so the replay can only close when the pre-remediation live state already equalled the after-image. Both records report APPLIED individually yet the whole scope is diverged. The Sprint 1 harness hides this because every multi-record case hand-resets debt[0].origin=1 before remediating, so the first base coincides with the after-image by construction.
adrs.decision: The replay remains the trust root (T2.1 finding 1 is deliberately not fixed in T2.1), but a genuine chain whose first record's base is the drifted live state must still certify. Concretely: resolveRemediationRebase must prove the first record's base is consistent with the live state it was built against rather than demanding it equal the checkpoint after-image, while still failing closed on hand-written records whose digests correspond to no state Kyro can reproduce. The existing QA probes (forged chain, no-op remediation over tampered state) define the attack boundary that any fix must keep failing closed.
consequences: A scope whose corruption predates its first remediation can present an honest multi-record chain as remediated instead of diverged.

The fix touches Sprint 1 replay code shared by doctor and the T2.1 derivation, so it must be validated with honest-path multi-record probes from a genuinely drifted base, not just the after-image-aligned fixtures.
alternatives: Relax the derivation to accept any per-record-APPLIED chain without replay — rejected, it lets a hand-written record whose base digests match nothing certify a diverged scope, which is exactly the QA probe 2 defect from Sprint 1.

Keep the strict after-image replay and document that legitimate first-record drift is unrepresentable — rejected, it makes the motivating case (corrupt-after-close) permanently divergent and forces operators to fabricate an after-image-aligned base.

adrs.title: Conform Lens provenance verification to Kyro v1 vectors
adrs.context: Lens must report valid remediation and recertification provenance without reusing the mutable Kyro runtime or trusting anchors alone.
adrs.decision: Lens implements a strict v1 verifier with canonical SHA-256 and checked-in real Kyro conformance vectors; cryptographic unavailability or any unsupported condition is reported as unsupported, and valid provenance is not inferred from anchor shape alone.
consequences: Reader-specific loading stays read-only and deterministic while verification semantics are explicit and regression-tested across runtimes.
The initial Lens verifier covers only declared v1 vectors; protocol evolution requires new vectors and an explicit version decision.
alternatives: Trust the anchor fields without verifying record, evidence, and chain semantics.
Import Kyro AI source or require a sibling checkout in Lens CI.

roadmap.sizingRationale: Three sprints isolate the persistence/security foundation, the verification and certification semantics, and the cross-repository Lens reader contract. Fewer sprints would mix irreversible writer behavior with its auditor and reader; more would create artificial boundaries. Sprint 2 depends on Sprint 1's stable remediation schema, and Sprint 3 depends on the finalized Doctor/status protocol.

sprints.title: Typed remediation protocol and atomic writer

recommendations: Sprint 2 (R5) should replace the current binary checkpoint verdict with the real state vocabulary: historical, remediated, recertified, diverged, unsupported. Today a legacy checkpoint that embeds a value the current schema rejects stays permanently invalid to doctor even after its live state is correctly remediated.
kyro recertify (R6) closes debt-1: check:cli-verbs fails only on that unshipped verb referenced in docs/plans/append-only-scope-remediation.md.

Before Lens ingestion (R7), confirm Lens resolves remediation records through remediations[].path — E3 made that field authoritative by binding it to the anchor id, and the reader must agree with doctor about which file is the evidence.
Re-run an independent QA certification of this scope when budget allows; the closing audit was performed by the same session that wrote the code.

Resolve debt-2 first: verify stateDigest(record.result.snapshot) === record.result.stateSha256 inside the replay loop, or drop snapshot and replay from the computed next state. It is not exploitable today only because chainContinuityIssue runs first.
Certify a global install, not just the local checkout. The installed runtime did not surface the verification state, which is what made the active-sprint false DIVERGED easy to miss.
Close S3/Lens and the R7 coverage that analyze still reports as pending before certifying the scope end to end.
